title: MessagingTemplate
description: An organisation's own message template, which a MessagingRoute uses instead of the system template for the event type. One template renders for every provider: Slack, Teams, Discord and Google Chat get the title, summary, body, fields, actions and accent; Jira and GitHub Issues get the issue fields; a signed webhook gets the rendered text and, when asked, the event payload. Every text field is a Go text/template run in a sandbox: only the messaging functions are allowed, every value is escaped, and sizes are capped. Plan compiles each field and refuses a template with errors. Every change to content is saved as a new version, noted as applied as code, as a console edit is; earlier versions stay in the template's history. Deleting it is refused while a route outside this apply still uses it.

displayName.description: The name the console shows, unique among the organisation's templates. Defaults to metadata.name.

eventScope.description: The event types the template is meant for: a type (scan.completed), a family (pix.*), or *. The console uses it to offer the template; a route may still use it for any event.

baseSystemTemplate.description: The key of the system template this one was copied from (generic, findings.report, scan.build_broken and so on). It is recorded so the console can say when that system template has a newer version; it does not change the content.

content.description: The template itself. Each text field is a template over the event view (.event, .subject, .actor, .data, .mentions, and .digest for a digest).

fields.description: Name and value pairs shown beside the body. At most 25.

inline.description: Show the field beside the previous one where the provider can.

actions.description: Buttons or links. At most 10. A URL that does not render to an https URL is dropped from the message.

accent.description: The colour bar: a severity (info, notice, warning, critical) or a #rrggbb colour, usually {{.event.severity}}.

issue.description: What an issue tracker target gets. A field left out falls back to the message's own.

labels.description: Labels to put on the issue. At most 10.

digest.description: How a batch of events is summed up when a route sends a digest.

title.description: The digest title, over the batch view (.digest.count).

item.description: One line per event in the batch.

webhook.description: What a signed webhook target receives.

includePayload.description: Send the event's payload, reduced to the fields the catalogue allows, beside the rendered text.

eventPattern.description: An event type (scan.completed), a family (pix.*), or * for every event.
